smells.finding: check_holdout_stability is the longest function (~30 lines of code, one loop body) but is a single cohesive algorithm (seed -> split -> pool -> fit -> compare -> record) with no mixed levels of abstraction; component_agreement_stat and main() are similarly short and single-purpose.
SplitResult/StabilityResult are frozen dataclasses (pure data records), no behavior; no class in this diff approaches large-class territory.
The two fit_property_mixture(rows_a, ...)/fit_property_mixture(rows_b, ...) calls in check_holdout_stability are structurally symmetric by necessity (compare A vs B), not duplicated logic to extract.

component_agreement_stat reads fit_a.scaler/fit_a.gmm.means_/fit_a.k from both fits, but this is a legitimate two-object comparator function, not a method on one class reaching into another's internals to do that class's own job -- MixtureFit is deliberately a data-only record (property_mixture.py docstring) with comparison logic living in the calling module, consistent with this codebase's pure-function-over-data-record pattern.
SplitResult's fields travel together as one meaningful record (a single split's outcome), not a clump repeated loose across multiple signatures.

radius_m/lateral_g stay plain floats/arrays here, matching corner_descriptors.py's (Gate 1) and property_mixture.py's (Gate 2) established convention for the same descriptor pair -- not a new primitive-obsession introduced by this diff, consistency with the existing pattern.
Max parameter count in this diff is 3 (check_holdout_stability: descriptors_by_circuit, n_splits, base_seed), all independently meaningful, no parameter object warranted.
This gate's new capability (F12 check) is self-contained in one new module + one new script + one new test file; no ripple of small edits across many unrelated files.

mixture_stability.py has exactly one reason to change (the held-out-stability statistic's own definition); f12_held_out_stability.py has one reason to change (how real grip_bin_obs data is wired into that statistic).

fit_a.scaler.inverse_transform(fit_a.gmm.means_) touches two attribute hops (fit_a.gmm.means_), but gmm/scaler/k are MixtureFit's own documented public surface (a deliberate DTO), and .means_ is sklearn's own GaussianMixture attribute name, not a chain through several internal collaborating domain objects.

No unused hooks, abstract base classes, or generalized parameters built for a hypothetical future case; hungarian_match/_json_safe are both used for exactly the one real need each currently serves (Infinity-token JSON safety is a concrete, documented, exercised requirement -- the real run produced float('inf') statistics).

The module docstring's extensive design-rationale prose (cross-fit-standardization resolution, threshold rationale, headline-verdict rule) explains WHY a non-obvious statistical/units decision was made -- required by the F12 falsifiable-gate mandate itself (rationale must be stated before the real run) -- not text papering over unclear code; the code beneath each explained decision is itself simple and readable on its own.
